questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The two lending mandates
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the stabilization mandate from the development mandate
questions.stem: OPS-1182 asks the treasury module to explain why lenders opened two separate facilities after the war, and which goal each one served.

options.text: Both facilities pursued the same objective and differed only in the interest rate charged to borrowers
options.misconception: believes both mandates were one goal sold at two prices

options.text: Stabilization lending covered short-term foreign exchange needs, development lending financed long investment
Stabilization lending built ports and power stations while development lending covered short-term bills
options.misconception: swaps the mandates by attaching the wrong time horizon

options.text: Both facilities were temporary reconstruction schemes that closed once the rebuilding phase had been completed
options.misconception: treats both mandates as temporary reconstruction spending

questions.explanation: Stabilization lending covered short-term foreign exchange needs while development lending financed longer investment. The two were neither one goal nor temporary reconstruction schemes.
questions.hint: Separate the facilities by time horizon, not by name.

Both suffer equally, because a price fall always lowers export earnings by the same percentage

questions.topic: A currency that outlived the colony
questions.learningObjective: Explain from a primary-style source why a colonial currency kept circulating after independence

stimulus.body: Customers may continue to deposit the notes of the former issuing authority at our branches until further notice. Balances so credited will be converted into the new unit at the same face value. No new notes of the old series will be issued.

questions.stem: DOC-61 attaches a bank circular to the ticket and asks what the quoted terms show about the pace of currency change.

options.text: The old notes were refused everywhere from the day the new unit was announced
options.misconception: claims immediate refusal despite the circular's terms

options.text: The old notes were still being issued by the banks after the change
options.misconception: ignores the statement that no new notes would be issued

options.text: The old notes stayed usable while acceptance ran out gradually rather than stopping at once
The new unit was worth less than the old notes at the same face value
options.misconception: misreads the equal face value as a devaluation

questions.explanation: The circular keeps old notes acceptable and stops new issuance, a managed transition rather than a clean break. Reading it as refusal, continued issuance or a changed value contradicts its terms.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why emergency loans carried conditions
questions.learningObjective: Explain why lenders attached conditions to emergency credit
questions.stem: SUP-477 asks the analyst to write a short account of why emergency loans carried conditions and why borrowers often resisted them.

answer.exemplar: An emergency loan was expected to be repaid, and repayment depended on the borrower's reserves holding up. Conditions on the exchange rate, imports and internal prices were the lender's way of making sure the adjustment happened before the money ran out. Borrowers resisted because each condition touched a constituency that would feel the squeeze first.

questions.explanation: A good answer links conditions to the lender's need for repayment and to the constituency that felt each one. Calling the terms hostile explains only half the conflict.
questions.hint: Explain lender protection and borrower resistance.

options.text: The unit eased strain, the break admitted the gap, and floating traded convertibility for flexibility

questions.explanation: A synthesis must run the three events in order and show what each contributed to the next. Reversing the order breaks the argument.
questions.hint: Order the events, then show what each changed.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why one commodity hurts one state more
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the same world price fall damages two exporters unequally
questions.stem: SUP-502 assigns the writer to explain plainly why one world price fall produces heavy damage in one country and little in another that exports the same commodity.

answer.exemplar: The world price is common to both exporters, but the damage is local. Where one commodity supplies most of national income, most tax receipts and nearly all foreign currency, a price fall removes a large share of every one of those at once. Where the commodity is a minor export, the same fall barely moves the budget, so the country can adjust without outside help.

questions.explanation: A full answer names the shared price shock and the different local exposures behind it. Answers that only restate the price fall miss the comparison.
questions.hint: Common price, different local share.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The two lending mandates
questions.learningObjective: Explain why lenders kept stabilization and development finance in separate facilities
questions.stem: SUP-540 wants a written account of why lenders kept two separate facilities instead of running one flexible fund for every kind of borrowing.

answer.exemplar: One fund would have to choose between two different jobs. Short-term foreign exchange support demanded quick decisions, firm conditions and repayment from a position of restored balances. Longer investment demanded patient appraisal of projects and a repayment schedule tied to project returns. Keeping them apart let each facility set its own conditions and its own pace.

questions.explanation: A good answer contrasts speed, conditionality and repayment basis between the two jobs. Listing both purposes alone misses why separation was useful.
questions.hint: Contrast conditions and pace, not just names.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why the gold link was cut in 1971
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a convertibility promise can stop working before it is formally ended
questions.stem: SUP-565 requests an account of why the promise to convert the reserve currency into gold stopped working before anyone announced its end.

answer.exemplar: Convertibility only works while holders believe it will be honoured. As the foreign-held amount of the currency grew past the metal available to redeem it, every holder became afraid to convert first, so nobody converted, gold stopped leaving the reserve, and the promise became hollow in practice before anyone announced its end.

questions.explanation: A strong answer explains the collective fear of converting first and the resulting paralysis of the promise. Stopping at gold scarcity leaves out the mechanism.
questions.hint: Explain why nobody converted, not just that gold was short.

questions.stem: BUG-1029 says the module treats a change of currency as an instant switch, and asks the team to correct the assumption.

options.text: A new currency takes effect at once, because the state can order every shop to change overnight

questions.topic: Why emergency loans carried conditions

questions.stem: SUP-588 wants a written account of why the conditions had to be agreed before emergency money was released rather than negotiated afterwards.

questions.topic: The two lending mandates
questions.learningObjective: Explain what separating the two facilities meant for borrowers and lenders
questions.stem: SUP-601 wants a written account of what separating stabilization from development finance meant in practice for the countries that borrowed.

answer.exemplar: Once the two facilities were apart, a country in payments trouble could ask for a short bridge without committing to a long programme, and a country with a viable project could seek long finance without first having to prove a payments crisis. questions.explanation: A good answer shows the practical gain in matching facility to need and in the specificity of conditions. Treating the separation as tidying misses what was gained.

questions.stem: SUP-633 wants a full account of why the conditions attached to emergency credit had to be ones the borrowing government could actually carry out.

answer.exemplar: A condition the borrower cannot deliver helps neither side. If the adjustment named in the clause was beyond the government's reach, the borrower would fail on paper as well as in fact, the lender would recover less than expected, and the next negotiation would start from a weaker position. Conditions that could be administered, measured and checked against real administrative capacity were the ones that protected both the repayment and the credibility of the agreement.

questions.explanation: A good answer connects the credibility of the terms to the borrower's capacity to deliver them and to the lender's recovery. Listing typical conditions misses that requirement.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why the gold link was cut in 1971
questions.learningObjective: Describe how the gold break changed the expectations of currency holders
questions.stem: OPS-1363 asks how the module should describe what the break in the gold link did to the expectations of people who held the currency.

options.text: They lost the promise of redemption at a stated rate and became exposed to exchange rate swings
They gained the promise of redemption, because the metal was committed to them in advance
options.misconception: inverts what holders gained from the break

options.text: Nothing changed for them, because the break applied only to governments and not to private holders
options.misconception: limits the break's effects to official holders

options.text: They were compensated, because the metal they gave up was returned in another form
options.misconception: invents a compensation that did not occur

questions.explanation: Holders of the currency moved from a stated redemption promise to exposure to a moving rate. Crediting them with a gain misstates what the break did.
questions.hint: Compare the old promise with the new position.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The reserve currency after floating
questions.learningObjective: Read a table of reserve composition to judge how the reserve currency's share moved
questions.stem: FEAT-329 shows a table of reserve composition before and after floating and asks the module to describe the change in the reserve currency's share.

options.text: The share fell to zero, so the currency played no part in settlement after floating
options.misconception: overstates the fall to zero without support

options.text: The share stayed identical, because floating changed only the label on the table
options.misconception: claims the composition did not change at all

options.text: The share fell but stayed substantial, so settlement use continued without a defended rate
The share grew, because floating made the currency attractive to holders of gold
options.misconception: invents a rise that the table does not show

questions.explanation: A falling share that remains substantial matches a currency still used for settlement. Reading the table as a fall to zero misstates what is recorded.
questions.hint: Ask what the share became, not only its direction.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The two lending mandates
questions.learningObjective: Explain how the two mandates reduced the lender's risk
questions.stem: BUG-1129 asks the team to explain why keeping the two facilities apart made lending to new states safer for the lender.

options.text: It let the lender spread its money over many borrowers, so no single failure could matter
options.misconception: claims a portfolio effect rather than a mandate effect

options.text: It let the lender judge each request against a clear purpose and attach terms suited to that purpose
It let the lender avoid the risk of lending at all, since both facilities were optional
options.misconception: claims the separation removed the need to lend

options.text: It let the lender charge a higher rate, which protected it from any loss on either facility
options.misconception: makes the price of credit the source of safety

questions.explanation: Separate mandates gave the lender a clear test for each request and terms matched to that risk. Portfolio spread or a higher rate misstate where the safety came from.
questions.hint: Ask what the lender could judge and attach.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The export structure inherited at independence
questions.learningObjective: Draw a conclusion about export dependence from an independence-era memo

stimulus.body: Our new country earns most of its foreign exchange from one crop sold to one market. When that price fell last year, our reserves fell with it, and no amount of administrative effort could raise revenue in time. We ask whether a loan could carry us through the low price.

questions.stem: DOC-138 attaches an independence-era memo to the ticket and asks which reading of it the module should offer.

options.text: The memo shows that administrative effort alone can widen the export base within a single season
options.misconception: reads administrative will as a stand-in for trade structure

options.text: The memo shows that reserve losses are unrelated to the price of a single export
options.misconception: denies that one export price drives reserve movements

options.text: The memo shows that only a formal loan agreement could have protected the reserves that year
options.misconception: claims a loan agreement was the only possible protection

options.text: The memo shows earnings concentrated in one crop and one market, exposing the country to a price fall

questions.explanation: The memo ties reserves directly to the price of a single crop sold to a single market. Reading administrative effort as the remedy ignores what the writer reports.
questions.hint: Quote the sentence that links reserves to one price.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Why one commodity hurts one state more
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a commodity price fall reaches a country's budget and its import bill
questions.stem: SUP-628 requests a written account of how one fall in a world commodity price reaches a country through two separate channels at the same time.

answer.exemplar: The first channel is fiscal. When the price of the main export falls, the earnings on which the government depends shrink, so tax receipts fall and any plan built on that revenue has to be cut or financed. The second channel is external. Foreign currency from the export is what pays for fuel, food and spare parts, so a lower price shortens the cover those imports can command, and the bill has to be met from reserves or a loan.

questions.explanation: A full answer names both channels, the shrinking public revenue and the shrinking import cover, and shows them acting together. Describing only one channel is incomplete.
questions.hint: Name both channels the price reaches.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A currency that outlived the colony
questions.learningObjective: Relate a surviving colonial currency to the state's external position
questions.stem: RFC-341 asks the team to relate the currency that outlived the colony to the state's external position and to the confidence of those who traded with it.

options.text: The currency set the state's trade balance, because its unit decided what imports were affordable
options.misconception: makes the unit of account drive the trade balance

options.text: The state's external position set the currency, which had no influence of its own
options.misconception: denies the currency any independent effect

options.text: The old unit stayed trusted because trade was already done in it, and that trust supported the state's credit
The currency and the external position were separate, and the note connecting them is coincidence
options.misconception: declares the connection accidental

questions.explanation: A synthesis must link the currency's continued acceptability to the flow of trade and from there to the state's standing with its creditors.
questions.hint: Show the link from trade to trust to credit.
